ns2:section.sectionText: ON-CAMPUS PROGRAM SECTION. Asynchronous online. No synchronous time/day. Canvas LMS. Enrollment Restrictions Notation: No late adds after start of first class without prior written permission of the professor at bmbarnet@illinois.edu. No Audit, Credit/No Credit, or Non-degree enrollments. Restricted to Graduate students with “Degree” status. Not for students with Freshman, Sophomore, Undergraduate Non-Degree, or Graduate Non-Degree class standing. Prerequisite: EPOL 409 Sociology of Education or written approval of the professor at bmbarnet@illinois.edu. Description: This seminar is a sociological, historical, and contemporary examination of the diversity of student-led protests of the 1960s (such as protest by activists in the Berkeley Free Speech Movement, Students for a Democratic Society, Student Non-Violent Coordinating Committee, Mexican American Youth Organization, Crusade for Justice, American Indian Movement, Asian American Political Alliance, Gay Liberation Front, Redstockings, Rolling Quads) and explores the differences and similarities between student protests of the 1960s/70s and protests in later decades to the present (such as #Occupy, #MeToo, #Black Lives Matter, #SayHerName, #Climate Change) and their impact on/in higher education. We will consider how students on and off college campuses have mobilized over free speech, civil rights, racism, sexism, heterosexism, ableism, militarism, poverty, women’s rights, LGBTQ+ rights, disability rights, immigrant rights, ethnic studies, women’s studies, multiculturalism, diversity in education, voting rights, military draft, ROTC, police violence, athlete pay, sports mascots, microaggressions, campus climates, tuition fees/costs, campus buildings and landmarks viewed as symbols of racism, undocumented and international students policies, among other issues. Prerequisite: EPOL 409 Sociology of Education or written approval of the professor at bmbarnet@illinois.edu.
